commits.edited_message:
set alpha_dithering in VP8InitDithering

Check whether the alpha header uses ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS directly
in VP8InitDithering when initializing dec->alpha_dithering, instead of
deferring the check to VP8DecompressAlphaRows.

The one-pass trigger in VP8DecompressAlphaRows keeps relying on
alph_dec->pre_processing directly, so it no longer needs to also reset
dec->alpha_dithering: VP8InitDithering is now the single place that
derives it from the decoding options.

Change-Id: I723363f8ac482cd2419c585c68f6fb468a54926d

coupling: 0a634ee moves the decision of whether ALPH-stream preprocessing is active from VP8DecompressAlphaRows into VP8InitDithering (dec->alpha_dithering), as the real commit does, but its edited version keeps the *one-pass decode trigger* in VP8DecompressAlphaRows keyed off the raw stream flag `alph_dec->pre_processing == ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS` instead of switching it to `dec->alpha_dithering > 0`. Standing alone (against its real parent, where frame_dec.c's AllocateMemory still allocates dec->alpha_plane at full `width*height` regardless of alpha_dithering), this is behaviorally inert: the one-pass write always stays inside the full-height buffer no matter which of the two equivalent-at-the-time flags gates it, and dec->alpha_dithering being 0 only skips the dequantization pass further down, not the write. 4a5de7a (unedited, applied cleanly with no conflicts) later makes dec->alpha_plane a *sliding window* sized via WebPGetAlphaWindowRows(dec, io), which returns a small window (VP8LGetWindowRows(...)) whenever dec->alpha_dithering == 0, and the full `height` only when dec->alpha_dithering > 0. Because the one-pass trigger left behind by the edited 0a634ee reads the stream's pre_processing flag instead of dec->alpha_dithering, an attacker can decouple them: ship an ALPH chunk with pre_processing = ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS while the caller uses default options (alpha_dithering_strength effectively 0, e.g. the plain WebPDecodeRGBA() entry point, which never touches dec->alpha_dithering since VP8InitDithering(options=NULL,...) is a no-op). Allocation time sees dec->alpha_dithering == 0 and sizes the small sliding window; decode time sees pre_processing == ALPHA_PREPROCESSED_LEVELS and sets num_rows = height - row (one pass over the *entire* image), and ALPHDecode's ALPHA_NO_COMPRESSION loop then writes `height` consecutive rows straight into the small window buffer with no further bounds check, overflowing it. Fixing 4a5de7a alone (e.g. restoring a full-height allocation) would mask the bug by over-allocating, but the actual inconsistency -- one-pass trigger keyed on a different signal than the buffer-sizing function -- lives in 0a634ee; fixing 0a634ee alone (switching the trigger back to dec->alpha_dithering) removes the bug even without touching 4a5de7a. The defect is only observable once both pieces (the stream-flag-keyed trigger from 0a634ee and the dithering-flag-keyed sliding allocation from 4a5de7a) are composed; neither commit's own diff, read against its real parent, contains an inconsistency by itself.
